record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For the longest increasing subsequence problem under non-uniform distributions on permutations or more general input distributions, do the fluctuations still satisfy KPZ-type universality, and how do those fluctuations behave?

evidence.quote: Also, regarding the original longest increasing subsequence problem, KPZ universality for the fluctuations has been proved so far only for the uniform distribution on the permutations: The problem for the fluctuations with more general distributions is very much open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, let $L_n(\sigma)$ denote the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $\sigma$, i.e., the largest $k$ such that there exist indices $i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k$ with $\sigma(i_1)<\sigma(i_2)<\dots<\sigma(i_k)$. When $\sigma$ is chosen uniformly at random from the symmetric group $S_n$, it is known (Baik–Deift–Johansson) that
$$\frac{L_n - 2\sqrt{n}}{n^{1/6}} \;\xrightarrow{d}\; F_2,$$
where $F_2$ is the Tracy–Widom GUE distribution, placing $L_n$ in the KPZ universality class.

Now let $\{\mu_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a family of probability measures on $S_n$ that is not the uniform measure (for instance, Mallows measures, Ewens measures, measures induced from i.i.d. samples of a continuous distribution via standardization but with non-product weights, or other natural non-uniform input distributions on permutations or on sequences from which an LIS is extracted). 

Determine, for as broad a class of such non-uniform measures $\mu_n$ as possible:
1. Whether there exist deterministic centering $a_n$ and scaling $b_n$ such that $(L_n - a_n)/b_n$ converges in distribution to a non-degenerate limit.
2. Whether this limit law is the Tracy–Widom GUE distribution $F_2$ (i.e., KPZ-type universality persists), or whether new limit laws and scaling exponents (possibly outside the KPZ class) arise.
3. Characterize the dependence of the centering, the scaling exponent, and the limit law on the underlying measure $\mu_n$.
artifact.category_tag: Longest increasing subsequences and KPZ universality
artifact.status_search_result: KPZ universality for the longest increasing subsequence is established for the uniform measure on permutations (Baik–Deift–Johansson, 1999) and various related integrable models. For non-uniform input distributions the picture is incomplete: results exist for specific families (e.g., Mallows permutations, certain random walks) showing both KPZ-type behavior in some regimes and non-universal behavior (e.g., non-$n^{1/2}$ scaling and non-Tracy–Widom limits) for heavy-tailed walks. A general characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: KPZ limit theorems (Baik, ICM survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of KPZ limit theorems centered on the uniform LIS case and integrable models.
status_evidence.claim: KPZ universality for LIS is established mainly for integrable/uniform settings.

status_evidence.title: Non-universality for longest increasing subsequence of a random walk
status_evidence.snippet: Symmetric ultra-fat tailed random walk has LIS asymptotically between n^0.690 and n^0.815, showing non-universality.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniform input distributions can yield non-KPZ scaling and unknown limit laws.

status_evidence.title: The scaling limit of the longest increasing subsequence (Dauvergne–Virág)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes scaling limit in the uniform/integrable regime.
status_evidence.claim: Progress concentrates on the uniform case; general non-uniform case is not covered.
